API Reference

ATProto.jl

A feature-complete AT Protocol SDK for Julia.

Overview

ATProto.ATProto — Module
ATProto

A Julia SDK for the AT Protocol (atproto.com), the decentralized social protocol powering Bluesky. Ported from the reference TypeScript and Go implementations maintained by the Bluesky team, together with community implementations.

See ROADMAP.md for the milestone plan. Current coverage:

  • ATProto.Syntax — identifier and primitive syntax types: DIDs, handles, NSIDs, TIDs, record keys, AT-URIs, datetimes, and language tags.
  • ATProto.Crypto — varints, multibase, multihashes, CIDs, did:key multikeys, and ECDSA (P-256 / secp256k1) via libcrypto.
source

Return true if s is a syntactically valid DID string (did:method:content, at most 2048 characters).

Return true if s is a syntactically valid TID (13 characters of the base32-sortable alphabet with the high bit unset).

source

is_valid_record_key(s) -> Bool

Return true if s is a valid record key (1–512 chars from A-Za-z0-9_~.:-, excluding "." and "..").

is_valid_at_identifier(s) -> Bool

Return true if s is a valid at-identifier — either a valid DID or a valid handle.

source
ATProto.Syntax.AtURI — Type
AtURI

An immutable, parsed AT-URI with a validated host (DID or handle).

Fields:

  • host::String — authority: a DID or handle
  • pathname::String — e.g. "/app.bsky.feed.post/3jx2h5l2b1c2p" (or "")
  • search_params::Vector{Pair{String,String}} — decoded query parameters
  • fragment::String — with a leading '#', or ""

Constructors:

  • AtURI(uri::AbstractString) — parse (throws InvalidAtUriError)
  • AtURI(uri::AbstractString; base) — parse relative to a base AT-URI
  • AtURI(host, collection, rkey) — build from parts (via at_uri)
source
ATProto.Syntax.at_uri — Function
at_uri(host, collection="", rkey="") -> AtURI

Build an AtURI from a host (handle or DID) and optional collection NSID and record key. collection may be an NSID and rkey may be a TID. Mirrors AtUri.make in the TypeScript reference.

source
ATProto.Syntax.is_valid_datetime — Function
is_valid_datetime(s) -> Bool

Return true if s is a valid atproto datetime string (RFC 3339 ∩ ISO 8601 ∩ HTML). No leap seconds; -00:00 is rejected; fractional seconds of any length are accepted.

source
ATProto.Syntax.datetime_string — Function
datetime_string(dt::DateTime) -> String

Serialize a DateTime (interpreted as UTC) to the canonical atproto format YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS.sssZ — millisecond precision, upper-case T and Z (mirrors JS Date.toISOString()).

source
ATProto.Syntax.parse_datetime — Function
parse_datetime(s) -> DateTime

Parse a valid atproto datetime string into a Dates.DateTime, converting numeric timezone offsets to UTC. Throws InvalidDatetimeError on invalid input.

NOTE: millisecond precision — Julia DateTime cannot represent finer fractional seconds.

source
ATProto.Syntax.NSID — Type
NSID

An immutable, validated NSID (Namespaced Identifier), e.g. "com.example.status".

Fields:

  • segments::Vector{String} — the period-separated parts

Construction validates the input and throws InvalidNsidError on invalid syntax. See also make_nsid and parse_nsid.

source
ATProto.Syntax.make_nsid — Function
make_nsid(authority, name) -> NSID

Build an NSID from a (non-reversed) domain authority and a name, e.g. make_nsid("example.com", "status") == NSID("com.example.status").

source
ATProto.Syntax.TID — Type
TID

An immutable, validated TID (Timestamp Identifier) — a 13-character base32-sortable string encoding a 64-bit integer (53-bit microsecond timestamp + 10-bit clock id, high bit zero).

Constructors:

  • TID(s::AbstractString) — validate and wrap a TID string
  • TID(u::UInt64) — encode a raw 64-bit TID value
  • TID(dt::DateTime; clockid=0) — build from a timestamp
  • TID(; clockid=0) — build from the current UTC time

Crypto

Multibase, CID, hashing, ECDSA.

ATProto.Crypto.multibase_to_bytes — Function
multibase_to_bytes(mb::AbstractString) -> Vector{UInt8}

Decode a multibase-prefixed string (first character selects the encoding) to bytes. Supported prefixes: f/F (base16), b/B (base32), z (base58btc), m/M (base64), u/U (base64url). Throws InvalidMultibaseError on an unsupported prefix or bad payload.

source
ATProto.Crypto.bytes_to_multibase — Function
bytes_to_multibase(bytes; encoding::Symbol=:base58btc) -> String

Encode bytes to a multibase-prefixed string. encoding is one of :base16, :base16upper, :base32, :base32upper, :base58btc, :base64, :base64pad, :base64url, :base64urlpad.

source
ATProto.Crypto.CID — Type
CID

An immutable, validated IPLD Content Identifier.

Fields:

  • version::UInt8 — 0 (implicit dag-pb) or 1
  • codec::UInt64 — multicodec code (DAG_CBOR_CODEC, RAW_CODEC, …)
  • digest::Vector{UInt8} — full multihash bytes (code + length + hash)

CIDs are equal when their codec and digest are equal (CIDv0 is equivalent to a CIDv1 with the dag-pb codec and the same digest, matching multiformats semantics).

source
ATProto.Crypto.cid_parse — Function
cid_parse(s) -> CID

Parse a CID string: a base58btc Qm... string (CIDv0) or a multibase-prefixed CIDv1 (b... base32 by atproto convention; z, u, f, … also accepted).

source
ATProto.Crypto.cid_for_dagcbor — Function
cid_for_dagcbor(block_bytes) -> CID

The CIDv1 (dag-cbor, sha2-256) for a serialized block — the standard CID used throughout atproto repositories.

source
ATProto.Crypto.sha256 — Function
sha256(data) -> Vector{UInt8}

SHA-256 digest of bytes (or of a UTF-8 encoded string). Uses the Julia SHA stdlib, same values as the TS reference's @noble/hashes sha256.

source
ATProto.Crypto.ripemd160 — Function
ripemd160(data) -> Vector{UInt8}

RIPEMD-160 digest (20 bytes) of bytes or a UTF-8 string. Pure Julia, validated against the official test vectors.

source
ATProto.Crypto.parse_did_key — Function
parse_did_key(did) -> NamedTuple

Parse a did:key:z... DID into (jwt_alg, key_bytes) where key_bytes is the uncompressed public key. Throws InvalidMultikeyError / UnsupportedKeyTypeError on bad input.

source
ATProto.Crypto.format_did_key — Function
format_did_key(jwt_alg, key_bytes) -> String

Format an uncompressed public key (P-256 or secp256k1) as a did:key:z... string, exactly matching formatDidKey in the TS reference.

source
ATProto.Crypto.P256Key — Type
P256Key

A P-256 (prime256v1 / ES256) ECDSA keypair or public key. See generate_key, import_key.

source
ATProto.Crypto.Secp256k1Key — Type
Secp256k1Key

A secp256k1 (ES256K) ECDSA keypair or public key. See generate_key, import_key.

source
ATProto.Crypto.generate_key — Function
generate_key(::Type{K}) where {K<:AbstractEcKey} -> K

Generate a fresh random keypair (P256Key or Secp256k1Key) using OpenSSL.

source
ATProto.Crypto.import_key — Function
import_key(::Type{K}, private_key) -> K where {K<:AbstractEcKey}

Import a 32-byte (or 64-char hex) private key and derive its public key.

source
ATProto.Crypto.sign_message — Function
sign_message(key, msg) -> Vector{UInt8}

SHA-256 hash msg and sign the digest (as in the TS reference): 64-byte compact, low-S signature.

source
ATProto.Crypto.verify_sig — Function
verify_sig(public_key, msg, sig; jwt_alg, allow_malleable=false) -> Bool

Verify a compact ECDSA signature of msg (SHA-256 hashed) against a public key. Strict by default: exactly 64-byte compact signatures and low-S values. jwt_alg is "ES256" (P-256) or "ES256K" (secp256k1).

source
ATProto.Crypto.recover_pubkey — Function
recover_pubkey(digest, sig65) -> Vector{UInt8}

Recover the uncompressed secp256k1 public key from a 65-byte recoverable signature (r ‖ s ‖ recovery_id) over a 32-byte digest.

Throws ArgumentError for malformed signatures or an invalid recovery id (matches libsecp256k1 behavior: no candidate key exists for the given id).

DAG-CBOR

Canonical CBOR encoding/decoding with CID support.

ATProto.DagCbor.dag_cbor_encode — Function
dag_cbor_encode(value) -> Vector{UInt8}

Encode a value into canonical DAG-CBOR bytes.

Accepted value types:

  • nothing → null; Bool → true/false
  • Int64/UInt64 (and Integers that fit; BigInt in native range only — bignum tags are forbidden by the DAG-CBOR spec)
  • Float64 only (rejects Float16/Float32 to keep encodings canonical)
  • String/AbstractString (UTF-8 text)
  • DagBytes → byte strings
  • CID → tag 42 links
  • AbstractVector → arrays
  • AbstractDict with String keys, or NamedTuple → maps (keys are re-sorted canonically)

Throws ArgumentError for anything else.

source
ATProto.DagCbor.dag_cbor_decode — Function
dag_cbor_decode(bytes) -> Any

Decode a single canonical DAG-CBOR value from bytes. Throws an error (a DAG-CBOR decode error) on malformed, non-canonical, or trailing input.

Value mapping: integers → Int64/UInt64, floats → Float64, text → String, byte strings → DagBytes, booleans → Bool, null → nothing, arrays → Vector{Any}, maps → Dict{String,Any}, links → CID.

source
ATProto.DagCbor.DagBytes — Type
DagBytes(bytes) <: Any

A byte-string value in the DAG-CBOR data model. Wraps Vector{UInt8} so that byte strings stay distinct from arrays of small integers (in TS the Uint8Array type plays this role; in Julia Vector{UInt8} alone would be ambiguous with arrays of CBOR integers).

source

source

ATProto.DID.DidResolver — Type
DidResolver(; plc_url, timeout, cache, fetch)

Dispatching DID resolver: did:plc → plc.directory, did:web → well-known. Supports the same stale-while-revalidate caching as the TS reference.

source
ATProto.DID.resolve_document — Function
resolve_document(r, did; force_refresh=false) -> Union{DidDocument, Nothing}

Resolve a DID to its document, consulting the cache first (stale entries are served while a refresh happens in the background). nothing when the DID positively does not exist.

source
ATProto.DID.resolve_atproto_data — Function
resolve_atproto_data(r, did) -> AtprotoData

Resolve a DID and extract its atproto data (signing key, handle, PDS).

source
ATProto.DID.PlcClient — Type
PlcClient(; plc_url=DEFAULT_PLC_URL, timeout=3, fetch=default_fetch)

Read-only client for a plc.directory server: DID documents, operation history, and audit logs. The transport is injectable (see PlcResolver).

source
ATProto.DID.verify_legacy_create — Function
verify_legacy_create(op; expected_did=nothing) -> Bool

Verify a PLC LegacyCreate genesis operation (Dict with a recoverable sig): the recovered secp256k1 key must be a did:key listed in rotationKeys, and — when expected_did is given — the derived genesis DID must match.

source
ATProto.DID.verify_operation — Function
verify_operation(op, rotation_keys) -> Bool

Verify a PLC Operation or Tombstone (Dict with a sigs list): at least one compact signature must be valid against one of the rotation_keys (did:key:z... strings). The unsigned op is re-encoded canonically before hashing, exactly as plc.directory does.

Identity

Handle resolution and bidirectional identity verification.

ATProto.Identity.HandleResolver — Type
HandleResolver(; timeout=3, backup_nameservers=nothing, fetch=default_fetch,
                 resolve_dns=resolve_handle_dns)

Resolves handles to DIDs:

  1. _atproto.<handle> DNS TXT records (via the system resolver)
  2. https://<handle>/.well-known/atproto-did (first line, did= prefixed)
  3. backup nameservers, if configured

Both fetch (HTTP transport) and resolve_dns are injectable for tests.

source
ATProto.Identity.resolve_handle — Function
resolve_handle(r, handle) -> Union{String, Nothing}

Resolve a handle to a DID (DNS TXT, then well-known HTTP, then backup nameservers). nothing when the handle has no valid atproto record.

source
ATProto.Identity.IdResolver — Type
IdResolver(; plc_url, timeout, did_cache, fetch, backup_nameservers, resolve_dns)

The top-level identity resolver: a DID.DidResolver plus a HandleResolver sharing configuration.

source
ATProto.Identity.resolve_identity — Function
resolve_identity(r, handle; force_refresh=false) -> String

Full bidirectional identity resolution (atproto spec): resolve the handle to a DID, resolve the DID's document, and verify the document's alsoKnownAs handle matches (case-insensitively). Returns the verified DID.

Throws HandleNotFoundError when the handle does not resolve, and IdentityMismatchError when the DID document declares a different handle.

source

Facet detection and text manipulation.

ATProto.RichText — Module
RichText(text; facets=nothing, clean_newlines=false)

A rich text: the text plus facets over UTF-8 byte ranges. Facets are sorted and zero/negative-length ones filtered. Supports insert/delete with facet index adjustment, detection, and segment iteration.

source

detect_facets(text::UnicodeString; agent=nothing) -> Union{Vector{Dict}, Nothing}

Detect mentions (@handle), links (URLs and bare domains), tags (#tag), and cashtags ($TICK) in text. Returns facet dicts with 0-based UTF-8 byte indices. When agent is given, mention handles are resolved to DIDs via com.atproto.identity.resolveHandle.

insert_text!(rt, insert_index, insert_text)

OAuth

PKCE, DPoP, JWT.

ATProto.OAuth.generate_pkce — Function
generate_pkce(byte_length=32) -> NamedTuple

Generate a PKCE pair: (verifier = "...", challenge = "...", method = "S256"). The verifier is a base64url-encoded random byte string (43-128 chars); the challenge is the base64url-encoded SHA-256 of the verifier.

source
ATProto.OAuth.generate_dpop_key — Function
generate_dpop_key(; alg="ES256K")

Generate a fresh DPoP key. atproto primarily uses ES256K (secp256k1); ES256 (P-256) is the fallback per the spec.

source
ATProto.OAuth.build_dpop_proof — Function
build_dpop_proof(key, method, url; nonce=nothing, access_token=nothing) -> String

Build a DPoP proof JWT (RFC 9449 §4.2) for an HTTP request. The proof is bound to the HTTP method (htm), the target URI without query/fragment (htu), an optional server nonce, and the base64url hash of the access token (ath) when present.

Returns a compact JWT signed with the key's algorithm (ES256 or ES256K).

source
ATProto.OAuth.OAuthClientMetadata — Type
OAuthClientMetadata(; kwargs...)

Validated OAuth client metadata (RFC 7591 + atproto spec). Required: client_id, redirect_uris. Must include "atproto" scope, "code" response type, and "authorization_code" grant type.

source
ATProto.OAuth.validate_client_metadata — Function
validate_client_metadata(meta) -> OAuthClientMetadata

Validate client metadata per the atproto OAuth spec:

  • must include the atproto scope
  • response_types must include code
  • grant_types must include authorization_code
  • token_endpoint_auth_method must be none or private_key_jwt
source

build_authorization_url(authorization_endpoint, client_id, redirect_uri;

Build the authorization URL the user should be redirected to.

source
ATProto.OAuth.exchange_code — Function
exchange_code(token_endpoint, client_id, redirect_uri, code, verifier;

Exchange an authorization code for tokens (RFC 6749 §4.1.3), DPoP-bound when a dpop_key is provided.

source
ATProto.OAuth.OAuthSession — Type
OAuthSession

An authenticated OAuth session: tokens + DPoP key + server metadata. Makes DPoP-bound requests to resource servers (PDS) and refreshes tokens on 401.

source
ATProto.OAuth.oauth_request — Function
oauth_request(session, method, url, body=nothing; headers=[]) -> HTTP.Response

Make a DPoP-bound request with the session's access token. On 401 with an use_dpop_nonce error, retries with the fresh nonce. On invalid_token, refreshes and retries.

ATProto.Jetstream.jetstream_subscribe — Function
jetstream_subscribe(f, url; cursor=nothing, wanted_collections=nothing,
                    wanted_dids=nothing, max_reconnects=10, backoff_min=1.0,
                    backoff_max=30.0, compression=nothing)

Subscribe to a jetstream/firehose WebSocket, calling f(event) for each decoded event. Automatically reconnects with exponential backoff (capped), resuming from the last seen cursor.

Filters:

  • wanted_collections: only these NSIDs (e.g. ["app.bsky.feed.post"])
  • wanted_dids: only these DIDs

The loop runs until the callback returns :stop, max_reconnects is exhausted, or the connection closes cleanly. Returns the last cursor seen.
